summary: Chat completions: spike in time-to-first-token after runtime kernel and quantization changes
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports a sudden increase in Time-To-First-Token (TTFB) for chat completion requests after an internal runtime update and a model re-pin to a quantized variant. Impact: interactive chat flows stutter for end users (long pauses before initial token).

Impact:
- Affects StreamlineAI production dedicated pool serving interactive chat UI.
- Average TTFB increased from ~80ms to ~650ms for first token (p50->p95 regressions).
- User-facing errors: timeouts in UI when clients have short streaming timeouts.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool (customer-dedicated-345) in us-east-1.
- Model pinned this morning to redwood/open-chat-7b-v2-q4_0 (quantized).
- Runtime rollout: serving-runtime v1.13.2 with new kernel selector and quant packing changes deployed at 2026-03-10 03:40 UTC.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a chat completion request with a 1-3 token system prompt then short user prompt (replicate customer workload).
2) Observe streaming connection and time to first token (TTFB) on new runtime.
3) Compare to same request pinned to unquantized model or prior runtime version.

Observed behavior:
- First token emitted after ~400-900ms depending on sequence length; subsequent tokens stream normally at expected rate.
- CPU/GPU traces show a heavy synchronous compilation/pack step during first token path.
- No steady-state throughput degradation once KV cache warm.

Expected behavior:
- TTFB similar to pre-update baseline (~<150ms p95) for the same request distribution.

Recent changes (possible leads):
- Serving-runtime v1.13.2 includes new kernel selection heuristics and a change to quantization packing which moves some per-request work to the first-token critical path.
- Models re-pinned to q4_0 quantized variants at customer request to reduce token cost.
- Scheduler autoscale tweak to reduce prewarm count for dedicated pools to optimize costs (may reduce hot workers).

Relevant logs / traces (excerpts):
[2026-03-10T04:12:03Z] request_id=sr-8b12 kernel-selector: selected kernel=matmul_v3_fused reason="quant_packed_preference"
[2026-03-10T04:12:03Z] request_id=sr-8b12 quant-pack: performed dynamic-packing on-shard=0 duration_ms=432
[2026-03-10T04:12:03Z] request_id=sr-8b12 first-token: compile/pack path added 445ms to critical path

Perf traces/links:
- Perf trace: https://perf.redwood.ai/trace/2026/03/10/sr-8b12
- Monitoring dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ttfb/serving-runtime-1_13_2

Notes:
- Customer verified issue appeared immediately after pin + runtime rollout window.
- Requests that hit a warm worker (recently used instance) show normal TTFB; cold-worker first requests show regression, suggesting increased first-request work.

Investigation summary:
- Hypothesis A: quant-pack dynamic work was moved to synchronous first-token path in v1.13.2; this adds ~300-500ms on cold workers.
- Hypothesis B: kernel selector prefers a new fused kernel that triggers slow JIT/compile on first use for certain sequence lengths; subsequent calls are fast.
- Checked scheduler: prewarm reduced from 2->1 for this dedicated pool 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC; fewer hot workers increases cold-start frequency.
- GPU trace shows large memcpy + unpack step tied to quant-packed tensors during first token generation.

Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Roll back kernel-selector change in serving-runtime for dedicated pools (safe fallback) OR force model to use unquantized variant until patch is released.
- Increase prewarm count for customer-dedicated-345 to 3 as a short-term countermeasure to reduce cold hits.
- Add a config flag to defer quant-pack to background thread (engineering fix).

Longer-term actions:
- Patch PR to move quant packing off of critical path (PR: github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/4875).
- Add performance regression test in CI that measures TTFB for first token across quantized and unquantized variants.
- Update rollout checklist to include dedicated-pool prewarm validation for kernel/compile-affecting changes.

Status update: Eng investigating kernel-selector fallback and quant pack path. Customer notified and prewarm increase applied as workaround on 2026-03-11.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:01 UTC - StreamlineAI (customer): We're seeing long pauses before the first token in our chat UI. This started after we pinned to q4 model and you mentioned a runtime update earlier today. UX timeouts happening frequently.
2026-03-10 09:17 UTC - Support (Aisha): Thanks for reporting — creating SUP-9187 and escalating to SRE/Eng. Can you provide example request IDs and approximate percent of sessions affected?
2026-03-10 09:29 UTC - StreamlineAI: Sample request IDs: sr-8b12, sr-8b13. ~22% of sessions experiencing a >300ms initial pause. We rolled model pin at 03:45 UTC this morning.

2026-03-10 12:05 UTC - SRE (Marco): Collected traces and saw a large dyn-pack step in first-token path. Scheduler prewarm for the dedicated pool was lowered yesterday; increasing prewarm as interim. Assigned to runtime team for kernel-selector review.

2026-03-11 02:40 UTC - Runtime Eng (Leah): Reproduced locally with v1.13.2 + q4 pack. Quant pack moved inline in a refactor; moving it to async should remove the extra latency. Preparing PR. Will also add a fallback to older kernel on first N requests.
2026-03-11 08:12 UTC - Support (Aisha): Applied prewarm increase for customer-dedicated-345. Customer to monitor and report back if TTFB improves for new sessions.

2026-03-12 15:20 UTC - StreamlineAI: After prewarm increase we see TTFB p95 drop to ~190ms for most sessions. Still occasional spikes when pool autoscaler terminates idle nodes. Please advise next steps.

2026-03-13 11:03 UTC - Runtime Eng (Marco): Merged interim fix to skip inline pack on first-token critical path (PR 4875). Will stage rollout to dedicated pools starting 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC with canary 5% then 25% then 100%.

2026-03-14 09:45 UTC - Support (Aisha): Notified customer of planned rollout and added monitoring alert to watch TTFB regressions. Marking ticket In Progress while rollout completes and we validate customer improvement.
investigation: Logs and traces point to quant-pack dynamic packing and a new kernel selection path added in v1.13.2 that perform compile/unpack work synchronously on the first token. Warm workers behave normally. Scheduler prewarm reduction exacerbated problem by increasing frequency of cold workers. Eng has a patch to move pack to background and added fallback for kernel selection.
resolution: Mitigations applied: increased prewarm for the dedicated pool (2026-03-11) and interim runtime fix merged (PR 4875) to remove quant-pack from the first-token critical path. Rollout scheduled and customer observed p95 improvement after prewarm. Follow-ups: full performance regression test in CI and a permanent kernel-selector safety revert if regression recurs.
resolution_notes: Customer confirmed initial latency improvement after prewarm bump. Full validation pending post-rollout of merged fix. Engineering to monitor for two days post-100% rollout and close ticket on confirmation.
